title: Encrypt Service-to-Service Traffic
description:
**SITUATION:**

Security wants payment calls encrypted **between Pods**, not only at the edge. TLS on Ingress helps browsers; it does not protect Order Processor → Payment Handler inside the cluster. A **service mesh** can add mutual TLS (each side proves who it is) without rewriting app code.

This lab turns on **mesh mTLS** so Order Processor → Payment Handler is encrypted in the cluster. Edge TLS alone is not enough; you are securing east-west traffic without rewriting app code.
**YOUR TASK:**

1. Enable mesh sidecar injection for the workloads that talk to each other (per platform instructions).
2. Apply a mesh policy so **Order Processor → Payment Handler** requires **mutual TLS**.
3. Verify Payment Handler still receives traffic from Order Processor (and plaintext from non-mesh clients is rejected if the platform supports that check).

**SPEC:**

- Workloads: `order-processor-deploy`, `payment-handler` (or their mesh-injected equivalents)
- Peer authentication / mTLS mode: **STRICT** (or Linkerd equivalent “require mTLS”) for Payment Handler (and optionally the whole namespace)
- Destination: Service `handler` on port **8000**
- Success: mesh dashboards / `proxy` logs / platform check show mTLS; apps remain Ready

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- Manifests: `mesh-mtls-l35.yaml` (PeerAuthentication / DestinationRule / Linkerd `Server`+`ServerAuthorization` — match the installed mesh).
- Do **not** terminate TLS only on Ingress and call that “mesh mTLS.”
- Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.

problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Encrypt Service-to-Service Traffic

Stay in your lab namespace. Turn on mesh sidecar injection and require **STRICT** mTLS for Payment Handler (Order Processor → handler on port 8000).

Docs: [Istio PeerAuthentication](https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/security/peer_authentication/) · [DestinationRule](https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/networking/destination-rule/)

## Solution YAML

Save as `mesh-mtls-l35.yaml` (Istio). Enable injection on the two workloads first by adding the pod-template label `sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true"` (the lab namespace itself is platform-managed, so label the workloads rather than the namespace).

```yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: payment-handler-strict
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-handler
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: payment-handler-mtls
spec:
  host: handler
  trafficPolicy:
    tls:
      mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL
```

If the platform uses Linkerd, use `Server` + `ServerAuthorization` requiring mTLS instead — match the installed mesh.

## Declarative

```bash
for d in order-processor-deploy payment-handler; do
  kubectl patch deploy "$d" --type merge \
    -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"sidecar.istio.io/inject":"true"}}}}}'
done
kubectl apply -f mesh-mtls-l35.yaml
kubectl rollout status deploy/order-processor-deploy
kubectl rollout status deploy/payment-handler
kubectl get peerauthentication,destinationrule
```

Wait until apps are Ready and the STRICT PeerAuthentication exists, then **Submit**. Do not call Ingress-only TLS “mesh mTLS.”
